title: The differential fibre and local cotangent space have equal dimension at a closed point
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], S a finite type k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and m a maximal ideal of S. Put R=S_m and K=kappa(m)=R/n, where n is the maximal ideal of R [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then the finite dimension over K of n/n^2 is equal to the finite dimension over K of K tensor_S Omega_{S/k} [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. This equality is independent of any bound involving Krull dimension.

proof.text: The map S -> K is surjective because m is maximal; hence K is finite type over k. Zariski's lemma makes K finite over k, and algebraic closedness makes k -> K bijective. Its inverse followed by k -> R is a k-algebra section of R -> K.

Reduce the section modulo n^2. The split conormal construction gives a retraction of n/n^2 -> K tensor_R Omega_{R/k}. Mathlib packages the square-zero retraction and the differential comparison modulo the square in retractionKerCotangentToTensorEquivSection. This proves injectivity. Exactness of the conormal sequence and Omega_{K/k}=0 prove surjectivity. Since R -> K is surjective, the resulting R-linear isomorphism is K-linear.

source.place: Lemma 00TR, split conormal sequence; Lemmas 02HP, 02HQ and 00RU

proof.text: Localization gives Omega_{R/k} = R tensor_S Omega_{S/k}. Tensoring this linear equivalence with K and using tensor cancellation gives K tensor_R Omega_{R/k} = K tensor_S Omega_{S/k}. Taking finranks of the two K-linear equivalences yields the claimed equality.

theorem finrank_cotangentSpace_atMaximal_eq_differentials
    (k : Type u) (S : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    [IsAlgClosed k] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (m : Ideal S) (hm : m.IsMaximal) :
    Module.finrank (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime m))
        (IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace (Localization.AtPrime m)) =
      Module.finrank m.ResidueField (TensorProduct S m.ResidueField
        (KaehlerDifferential k S))
